newsitem.title: ESTONIA: INTERVIEW-RUHRGAS TO RAISE ITS STAKE IN ESTONIA, LATVIA.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-RUHRGAS TO RAISE ITS STAKE IN ESTONIA, LATVIA.

text.p: Germany's Ruhrgas wants to increase its stakes in Estonia and Latvia's gas companies to 25 percent in the long-term, the vice-president of Ruhrgas, Eberhard R. Kranz, said on Friday.
Ruhrgas has a 15 percent stake in Eesti Gaas (Estonian Gas), the natural gas distributor in Estonia. It bought 16.25 percent of Latvijas Gaze (Latvian Gas) earlier this month.
"The aim is to increase the stake up to 25 percent," Kranz told Reuters in an interview.
"Such a move is a long way off - not this year or next year... we will see what the market will show us," he said.

Kranz said the stake in Latvian gas distributor company will increase to 18.2 percent by the end of the year. Ruhrgas will pay the tax debt the company owes to state, which will be exchanged for shares, he said.
The Estonian and Latvian gas companies both also have Russia's Gazprom as a shareholder with 30.64 percent.
"In my opinion, both companies should cooperate in future more than they have in the past," Kranz said.
For example, he said Estonian Gas could make use of Latvian Gas' considerable storage facilities.

The two gas companies are also both planning to list their shares on their local stock exchanges. The private shares in Lithuania's state-run gas firm, Lithuanian Gas, are active on the Vilnius bourse.

The Estonian Privatization Agency will sell 12.33 percent of Estonian Gas' shares in May or June. In Latvia, the state wants to sell up to 30 percent of Latvian Gas to its employees, Latvian citizens through vouchers and to the Savings bank.
Kranz said Ruhrgas was also interested in Lithuanian Gas.
"We are in discussions to learn a little bit about the gas industry in Lithuania," he said.
The Lithuanian government has committed itself to selling off several energy firms but has yet to put Lithuanian Gas on its privatisation list.
German Ruhrgas had a turnover of 13 billion DM and a net profit of 662 million DM in 1996.
